subject.title: fix(security): close Host-header Origin spoof bypass in gateway browser origin check

question: Should OpenClaw retain configuration-free direct LAN/Tailnet same-origin Control UI access, or intentionally require every non-loopback client to configure an allowlist or dangerous fallback?
rationale: This is a public gateway security and compatibility boundary: the patch intentionally changes an established direct-network access path, while the asserted browser-CSRF exploit has not been demonstrated through a real browser-to-gateway request.

options.title: Retain direct private-network access
options.body: Keep the current private same-origin behavior and require a browser-grounded exploit trace before changing the established LAN/Tailnet contract.

options.title: Adopt strict non-local policy
options.body: Require `allowedOrigins` for all non-local clients, but first document release-level migration guidance and prove fresh, upgrade, direct-LAN, and reverse-proxy behavior.

recommendation.title: Retain direct private-network access
recommendation.body: Keep the current private same-origin behavior and require a browser-grounded exploit trace before changing the established LAN/Tailnet contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Likely routing point for a gateway security/compatibility decision affecting the public Control UI connection contract.
